claim: The p.R47H variant of TREM2 is an Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk factor.
source: To study the mechanisms by which the p.R47H variant of the microglia gene and Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk factor TREM2 increases dementia risk, we created Trem2R47H KI rats.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established context for the study.

claim: Pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present increased brain concentrations of TNF-α.
source: Interestingly, pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present increased brain concentrations of TNF-α, augmented glutamatergic transmission, suppression of Long-term-Potentiation (LTP), an electrophysiological surrogate of learning and memory, but normal Aβ levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present augmented glutamatergic transmission.
source: Interestingly, pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present increased brain concentrations of TNF-α, augmented glutamatergic transmission, suppression of Long-term-Potentiation (LTP), an electrophysiological surrogate of learning and memory, but normal Aβ levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present suppression of Long-term-Potentiation (LTP).
source: Interestingly, pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present increased brain concentrations of TNF-α, augmented glutamatergic transmission, suppression of Long-term-Potentiation (LTP), an electrophysiological surrogate of learning and memory, but normal Aβ levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 7.

claim: LTP is an electrophysiological surrogate of learning and memory.
source: Interestingly, pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present increased brain concentrations of TNF-α, augmented glutamatergic transmission, suppression of Long-term-Potentiation (LTP), an electrophysiological surrogate of learning and memory, but normal Aβ levels.
evidence: This is stated as established scientific knowledge.

claim: Pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats have normal Aβ levels.
source: Interestingly, pre- and peri-adolescent Trem2R47H rats present increased brain concentrations of TNF-α, augmented glutamatergic transmission, suppression of Long-term-Potentiation (LTP), an electrophysiological surrogate of learning and memory, but normal Aβ levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 1 and previously published data (Tambini and D'Adamio, 2020).

claim: Acute reduction of TNF-α activity with a neutralizing anti-TNF-α antibody occludes the boost in amplitude of glutamatergic transmission observed in young Trem2R47H/R47H rats.
source: Acute reduction of TNF-α activity with a neutralizing anti-TNF-α antibody occludes the boost in amplitude of glutamatergic transmission and LTP suppression observed in young Trem2R47H/R47H rats.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Acute reduction of TNF-α activity with a neutralizing anti-TNF-α antibody occludes LTP suppression observed in young Trem2R47H/R47H rats.
source: Acute reduction of TNF-α activity with a neutralizing anti-TNF-α antibody occludes the boost in amplitude of glutamatergic transmission and LTP suppression observed in young Trem2R47H/R47H rats.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The microglia-specific pathogenic Trem2 variant boosts glutamatergic neuronal transmission by increasing brain TNF-α concentrations.
source: Thus, the microglia-specific pathogenic Trem2 variant boosts glutamatergic neuronal transmission and suppresses LTP by increasing brain TNF-α concentrations, directly linking microglia to neuronal dysfunction.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined experimental data showing increased TNF-α and the reversal of glutamatergic changes with anti-TNF-α treatment.

claim: The microglia-specific pathogenic Trem2 variant suppresses LTP by increasing brain TNF-α concentrations.
source: Thus, the microglia-specific pathogenic Trem2 variant boosts glutamatergic neuronal transmission and suppresses LTP by increasing brain TNF-α concentrations, directly linking microglia to neuronal dysfunction.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined experimental data showing increased TNF-α and the reversal of LTP suppression with anti-TNF-α treatment.

claim: The Trem2R47H variant directly links microglia to neuronal dysfunction.
source: Thus, the microglia-specific pathogenic Trem2 variant boosts glutamatergic neuronal transmission and suppresses LTP by increasing brain TNF-α concentrations, directly linking microglia to neuronal dysfunction.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings showing that a microglia-specific gene variant affects neuronal function through TNF-α.

claim: AD is the most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder in the elderly.
source: AD, the most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder in the elderly, is diagnosed when clinical dementia occurs concomitantly with Aβ plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and neuronal loss (James et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and supported by citation.

claim: AD is diagnosed when clinical dementia occurs concomitantly with Aβ plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and neuronal loss.
source: AD, the most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder in the elderly, is diagnosed when clinical dementia occurs concomitantly with Aβ plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and neuronal loss (James et al., 2014).
evidence: This diagnostic criterion is supported by citation to James et al., 2014.

claim: Genome-wide association studies have discovered TREM2 human variants that increase the risk of developing sporadic AD.
source: Genome-wide association studies have discovered Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) human variants that increase the risk of developing sporadic AD (Guerreiro et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Guerreiro et al., 2013.

claim: In the central nervous system (CNS), TREM2 is exclusively expressed in microglia.
source: In the central nervous system (CNS), TREM2 is exclusively expressed in microglia (Schmid et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schmid et al., 2002.

claim: TREM2 genetic evidence directly implicates microglia function in AD pathogenesis.
source: This genetic evidence directly implicates microglia function in AD pathogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the exclusive expression of TREM2 in microglia and its association with AD risk.

claim: Microglia surround amyloid plaques in AD patients.
source: Microglia surround amyloid plaques both in AD patients (McGeer et al., 1987) and Aβ plaques-bearing mice (Frautschy et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to McGeer et al., 1987.

claim: Microglia surround Aβ plaques in Aβ plaques-bearing mice.
source: Microglia surround amyloid plaques both in AD patients (McGeer et al., 1987) and Aβ plaques-bearing mice (Frautschy et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Frautschy et al., 1998.

claim: Disease‐associated microglia (DAM) possess enhanced activities, including the Aβ plaque-clearing activity.
source: Recent data suggest that these disease‐associated microglia (DAM) possess enhanced activities, including the Aβ plaque-clearing activity (Keren-Shaul et al., 2017; Mazaheri et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Keren-Shaul et al., 2017 and Mazaheri et al., 2017.

claim: Disease‐associated TREM2 variants cause a loss of function of TREM2 through diverse mechanisms.
source: Through diverse mechanisms (Kleinberger et al., 2017; Mazaheri et al., 2017; Schlepckow et al., 2017; Song et al., 2018; Ulland et al., 2015), disease‐associated TREM2 variants cause a loss of function of TREM2 that inhibits microglia transition to DAMs and impairs Aβ plaque-clearing activities (Mazaheri et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Disease‐associated TREM2 variants inhibit microglia transition to DAMs.
source: Through diverse mechanisms (Kleinberger et al., 2017; Mazaheri et al., 2017; Schlepckow et al., 2017; Song et al., 2018; Ulland et al., 2015), disease‐associated TREM2 variants cause a loss of function of TREM2 that inhibits microglia transition to DAMs and impairs Aβ plaque-clearing activities (Mazaheri et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mazaheri et al., 2017.

claim: Disease‐associated TREM2 variants impair Aβ plaque-clearing activities.
source: Through diverse mechanisms (Kleinberger et al., 2017; Mazaheri et al., 2017; Schlepckow et al., 2017; Song et al., 2018; Ulland et al., 2015), disease‐associated TREM2 variants cause a loss of function of TREM2 that inhibits microglia transition to DAMs and impairs Aβ plaque-clearing activities (Mazaheri et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mazaheri et al., 2017.

claim: The p.R47H TREM2 variant destroys an essential lipid and Aβ-binding site within the TREM2 ectodomain.
source: As for the AD-associated p.R47H TREM2 variant, in vitro studies suggest that it destroys an essential lipid and Aβ-binding site within the TREM2 ectodomain, reducing the Aβ-phagocytosis capabilities of microglia (Yeh et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yeh et al., 2016 and is based on in vitro studies.

claim: The p.R47H TREM2 variant reduces the Aβ-phagocytosis capabilities of microglia.
source: As for the AD-associated p.R47H TREM2 variant, in vitro studies suggest that it destroys an essential lipid and Aβ-binding site within the TREM2 ectodomain, reducing the Aβ-phagocytosis capabilities of microglia (Yeh et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yeh et al., 2016 and is based on in vitro studies.

claim: Trem2R47H knock-in (KI) rats carry the p.R47H variant in the rat endogenous Trem2 gene.
source: Model organisms are useful tools to study how human pathogenic mutation/variants alter protein's functions and promote disease in humans; thus, to dissect the pathogenic mechanisms of the p.R47H TREM2 variant, we generated Trem2R47H knock-in (KI) rats, which carry the p.R47H variant in the rat endogenous Trem2 gene (Tambini and D'Adamio, 2020).
evidence: This is a description of the model organism generated for this study, supported by citation.

claim: Rat and human APP differ by 3 amino acids in the Aβ region.
source: Rat and human APP differ by 3 amino acids in the Aβ region.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the difference between rat and human APP.

claim: Human Aβ may have higher propensity to form toxic species as compared to rodent Aβ.
source: These differences may be crucial since human Aβ may have higher propensity to form toxic species as compared to rodent Aβ and the pathogenic role of the p.R47H TREM2 variant may be linked to toxic Aβ clearance deficits.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative possibility to justify the humanization of the rat Aβ sequence.

claim: The pathogenic role of the p.R47H TREM2 variant may be linked to toxic Aβ clearance deficits.
source: These differences may be crucial since human Aβ may have higher propensity to form toxic species as compared to rodent Aβ and the pathogenic role of the p.R47H TREM2 variant may be linked to toxic Aβ clearance deficits.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative hypothesis.

claim: Mutations were introduced to 'humanize' the rat Aβ sequence (Apph allele) in Trem2R47H KI rats.
source: To eliminate this potential issue, together with the Trem2 mutation we introduced mutations to 'humanize' the rat Aβ sequence (Apph allele) (Tambini et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the genetic modification made to the model, supported by citation.

claim: In Trem2R47H KI rats, transcription, splicing and translation of the pathogenic variant is controlled by endogenous regulatory elements.
source: In Trem2R47H KI rats, transcription, splicing and translation of this pathogenic variant is controlled by endogenous regulatory elements, allowing to study pathogenic mechanisms triggered by the p.R47H TREM2 variant in a model organism mimicking the genetics of the human disease and expressing physiological levels of human Aβ.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the model organism design.

claim: Pre-adolescent Trem2R47H rats showed no significant alterations in brain levels of human Aβ40 and Aβ42.
source: Pre-adolescent (Sengupta, 2013) Trem2R47H rats showed no significant alterations in brain levels of human Aβ40 and Aβ42, the latter is considered the pathogenic Aβ species (Tambini and D'Adamio, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Tambini and D'Adamio, 2020).

claim: Aβ42 is considered the pathogenic Aβ species.
source: Pre-adolescent (Sengupta, 2013) Trem2R47H rats showed no significant alterations in brain levels of human Aβ40 and Aβ42, the latter is considered the pathogenic Aβ species (Tambini and D'Adamio, 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: The Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio is not altered in pre-adolescent Trem2R47H rats.
source: In addition, the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio, another indicator of Aβ-mediated pathogenesis, is not altered.
evidence: This claim is supported by previous experimental data (Tambini and D'Adamio, 2020).

claim: The Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio is an indicator of Aβ-mediated pathogenesis.
source: In addition, the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio, another indicator of Aβ-mediated pathogenesis, is not altered.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: The consequences of the Aβ-clearance deficits caused by the p.R47H TREM2 variant likely fully manifest in vivo in an aging-dependent manner.
source: Thus, it is likely that the consequences of the Aβ-clearance deficits caused by the p.R47H TREM2 variant fully manifest in vivo in an aging-dependent manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of Aβ changes in young animals despite known clearance deficits.

claim: The p.R47H TREM2 may trigger both human Aβ-dependent and Aβ-independent pathogenic mechanisms.
source: Yet, the p.R47H TREM2 may trigger both human Aβ-dependent and Aβ-independent pathogenic mechanism.

claim: Aβ-independent mechanisms may precede and participate in mechanisms leading to dementia.
source: Aβ-independent mechanism may precede and, perhaps, participate in mechanisms leading to dementia.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative hypothesis.

claim: In macrophages, TREM2 functions to inhibit pro-inflammatory cytokines production, especially TNF-α.

evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Turnbull et al., 2006.

claim: Loss of TREM2 function caused by the p.R47H variant may favor pro-inflammatory cytokine production by microglia.
source: Thus, it is possible that loss of TREM2 function caused by the p.R47H variant may favor pro-inflammatory cytokine production by microglia.
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis based on known TREM2 function in macrophages.

source: No differences were seen in Aβ40 and Aβ42 levels and the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio between Trem2w/w, Trem2R47H/w, and Trem2R47H/R47H rats (Figure 1).

claim: No significant differences were seen in Aβ42 levels in the CSF between Trem2w/w, Trem2R47H/w, and Trem2R47H/R47H rats.

claim: No significant differences were seen in the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio in the CSF between Trem2w/w, Trem2R47H/w, and Trem2R47H/R47H rats.
source: No differences were seen in Aβ40 and Aβ42 levels and the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio between Trem2w/w, Trem2R47H/w, and Trem2R47H/R47H rats (Figure 1).

source: Macrophages lacking Trem2 produce more TNF-α in response to LPS, zymosan and CpG, suggesting that Trem2 functions to inhibit cytokine production by macrophages (Turnbull et al., 2006).

claim: Trem2 functions to inhibit cytokine production by macrophages.

claim: Physiological levels of TNF-α produced by glia cells are required for normal surface expression of AMPA receptors at synapses.

evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.
